text: Friday, the day before the raid. In a D-grade gate, a basalt-plated boar the size of a truck charges down a ruined aqueduct.
It slams into Borro's shield and shoves him back through the water.
The stone cracks under his heels. Both summons are in field form, linked.
Nib leaps onto its back, but his knives skid off the basalt in sparks.
The boar bucks him into the water and wheels away for another run.
Back by the gate, both impacts land in Jaeha at once.
Bomi sulks over her switched-off drone: the best fight of the year, and she can't film it. She signed his rules, says Choi.
No cameras today, Jaeha says, wiping his nose. Tomorrow the whole country gets to watch.
Nib climbs out, dripping. His knives can't get through: it's wearing a road. And Borro can stop it, but he can't hurt it.
Jaeha writes it down. Nib is fast but light. Borro is strong but slow. Neither is enough.
Far down the channel, the boar lowers its head.
Again! Borro holds, and Nib looks for a gap.
The next charge buckles Borro's shield.
And this time, Jaeha feels exactly where the force goes: in through Borro's link, down through his body, and out into the stone.
His eyes widen. It goes through him. He doesn't have to keep it.
What if he sends it on, into Nib's knife instead of the ground?
He walks out onto the cracked channel. Yerin protests that he's supposed to stay back. He needs to be closer.
He explains fast: when the boar hits Borro, he'll push the force into Nib's knife. Nib points out he's never done that.
Jaeha grins, a little mad. That's what a test is for.
The boar charges, and Nib crouches to spring.
Impact. A ragged pulse tears out of Jaeha toward Nib, but Nib jumped too early, and it scatters into sparks.
Nib's knife glances off, and a tusk rips across Borro's arm.
The same cut opens on Jaeha's forearm. His nose bleeds, his ears ring. Force transfer failed.
Yerin runs out onto the channel. Choi yells that the floor is cracking. So is he, she yells back.
As she heals him, Jaeha laughs weakly. For half a second, it worked. Nib was just too early.
Nib's field form runs out. One minute of cooldown.
Jaeha studies the charge. Its head drops three strides before it hits. Nib has to strike the instant it hits Borro.
So Nib stands on the shield. The hit comes in, and goes straight out through him.
Cooldown over. Nib climbs onto the rim of Borro's shield, eye flaring amber, and Jaeha lays a hand on Borro's shell.
If Nib falls off, Borro will not catch him. Nib doesn't fall.
The boar charges, and its head starts to drop.
Jaeha counts. Three. Two. One.
Impact. The force runs from the shield through Borro, through Jaeha's hand and body, and up the link into Nib, who drops onto the boar's skull with the pulse blazing down his arms.
The basalt splits open like broken paving.
The boar collapses into the water, its plates sliding off.
It dissolves into ash. Behind Borro, Jaeha has sunk to his knees.
His raised hand trembles violently, a white-gold glow fading from the skin.
Blood trickles from one ear. He's smiling anyway.
A big window: new skill, Pass. Move force between two linked summons, through the Operator. Each hand-off loses thirty percent.
And the cost, in red. The force passes through the Operator's body.
Nib looks at his knives. That was the boar's own weight behind them. He likes this. Do it again.
Borro holds up his dented shield, mournfully. Then Nib can take the next charge.
Nib with a pot-lid shield, sweating. Borro with a cup of tea, smug.
Bomi is in agony: the coolest thing she's ever seen, and she didn't film it. Good, says Choi. The less anyone sees before tomorrow, the better.
Yerin helps him up. His hands shake, his ear bleeds, and he just hit a boar with its own weight.
A violet core rises from the water.
Boss defeated. Harvest the core, three and a half million won. No other option.
He adds it to a list. Hound, alpha, serpent, boar. Only harvest, four times now. Why?
A new kind of boss, so Route Alignment climbs from ninety percent to one hundred.
And a huge window unfolds. A call is available. Two of three slots used. Speak, and the Far Side will hear his offer.
Yerin says call now, the night before the raid. Borro will make room under the tarp.
But Jaeha thinks it through. Sora watches for summons. Mok expects two. He planned for two.
His finger hovers over the button, then curls back.
He sweeps the window away. Not yet. He'll need it in there.
Nib gives a small nod, soldier to soldier. A scout always keeps one knife hidden.
Choi notes he can't even hold a cup. Tomorrow, Jaeha says, he'll be holding something else.
At the edge of his vision, one tiny mark stays pinned. Call: held.
They walk out into the noon light.
Tomorrow, Mok expects him to walk in first. And he will.
